hero.headline: Your media. Your library. Your Phlix.
hero.subheadline: An open-source PHP media server that streams to your Roku, Samsung TV, Windows desktop, phone, and any DLNA device — with SyncPlay, Live TV, transcoding, and a hub that follows you anywhere.

pitch_bullets: 100% self-hostable — your library never leaves your hardware unless you say so
Native clients on Roku, Samsung Tizen, Windows, Mobile, plus any DLNA device
Real-time SyncPlay with NTP-style time sync so movie night actually stays in sync
Multi-source metadata: TMDB, TVDB, Fanart.tv, and local NFO with 24-hour cache
Adaptive HLS streaming, FFmpeg transcoding, per-device quality profiles
Live TV with DVR + EPG guide integration
Plugin system with a versioned manifest contract

features.title: Library that organizes itself
features.body: Folder-watcher hashes mtimes, scanner parses S01E02 / (2020) titles, ItemRepository hydrates metadata_json. Add a file, see it appear.

features.title: SyncPlay across the room or across the country
features.body: Weighted-mean NTP offset over 5 samples keeps every device locked to the same frame. Play, pause, seek — everyone moves together.

features.title: Transcoding that picks the right quality
features.body: QualitySelector profiles for mobile-low, mobile-high, web, and tv-4k. CRF 23/28 libx264/libx265 with HLS master and variant playlists.

features.title: Multi-user, multi-profile, parental controls
features.body: JWT auth with refresh tokens, Argon2ID password hashing, up to 5 profiles per user, 4- or 6-digit PINs, rating filter from G to NC-17.

features.title: Live TV with DVR + EPG
features.body: ChannelManager, GuideManager, and Recorder give you scheduled recordings and a guide that doesn't make you click through menus.

features.title: DLNA for the devices you already own
features.body: ContentDirectory, AvTransport, and a DeviceRegistry mean your old smart TV doesn't need a new app.

features.title: Plugin system with a real contract
features.body: LifecycleInterface + manifest schema. Drop a plugin in, the loader picks it up. See phlix-plugin-example.

features.title: Phlix Hub — reach any of your servers from anywhere
features.body: Sign in once. Reverse-tunnel relay handles NAT. Self-hostable, or use the public hub.

ecosystem.name: phlix-server
ecosystem.what: The media server itself — PHP 8.3+, Workerman 5.x

ecosystem.name: phlix-shared
ecosystem.what: Shared interfaces, DTOs, event types — Composer package

faq.q: Is Phlix like Plex / Jellyfin / Emby?
faq.a: Yes — same job, different stack. Phlix is built in PHP 8.3+ on Workerman, ships with a versioned plugin contract, and includes a hub for accessing remote servers behind NAT without a third-party tunnel.

faq.q: Do I need to expose my server to the internet?
faq.a: No. Run Phlix on your LAN and use the Phlix Hub's reverse-tunnel relay to reach it from your phone or Roku at a friend's house. You can self-host the hub, or use the public one.
Anything FFmpeg can read. Direct play when the client supports it; transcoded HLS otherwise. Per-device quality profiles pick the right bitrate automatically.
Yes — React Native, available on iOS and Android. Currently in beta.
Yes. Implement LifecycleInterface, ship a manifest, drop it in the plugins directory. See phlix-plugin-example for the smallest working starter.

Phlix Server and the Hub are MPL-2.0 — open source, and you can build on them commercially. If you modify a Phlix file, that file stays open; anything you add alongside it is yours. The shared libraries, plugins, and clients are MIT so you can build on them freely.

meta.description: Self-hostable PHP media server with native apps for Roku, Samsung TV, Windows & mobile. SyncPlay, Live TV, DVR, DLNA support.
